summaryText:
Dr. Scott Williams, a guest speaker and friend of Impact Church, brought a Father's Day message titled "Change the Temperature" as part of the Change series. He began by reminding the church that words matter, pointing to Proverbs 18:21, and led everyone in the series declaration, inviting Jesus to change every area of life. He then anchored the message in 2 Corinthians 5:17, the promise that anyone in Christ is a new creation, and Proverbs 22:6, which speaks of training children in the way they should go.

Pastor Scott's main text was Ephesians 6:1-4, with a focus on verse 4. He explained that Paul describes spiritual order in the home: children obey and honor their parents "in the Lord," and fathers are called to lead without provoking their children to anger. He stressed that this word calls fathers up rather than calling them out. It points to a father's position and calling, not his past, and it is never too late to step into it.

His central picture was the difference between a thermometer, which only reads the temperature of a room, and a thermostat, which sets it. A "thermostat dad" does not simply react to the mood of the home but leads with wisdom, truth, and grace. He gave three ways a thermostat dad changes the temperature. First, he regulates, bringing steadiness and calm rather than provoking his children. Second, he cultivates, investing consistent time, honesty, and presence, since what we water grows and what we neglect withers. Third, he elevates, putting God first and treating his family as his primary ministry. Pastor Scott noted that no one has to be a perfect parent, and that the most important gift a parent can give is presence, not presents.

He spoke with care to those hurt by absent or inconsistent fathers. He shared that he grew up without a father in the home, and encouraged listeners that this can become an opportunity to break cycles rather than an excuse. He reminded everyone that our heavenly Father is steady and faithful no matter what an earthly father was like. He also encouraged the church to speak life to the people around them, sharing a brief story of encouraging a restaurant worker about Jesus.

The service closed with an invitation for fathers to come forward in surrender, with prayer for restored relationships, freedom from addiction, and release from shame. Pastor Scott then invited anyone who had never surrendered their life to Jesus to do so, and led the church in a prayer of salvation.
mainPoints: Thermostat dads regulate: they do not provoke their children to anger, but bring steadiness, wisdom, truth, and grace into the home instead of just reacting to the mood of the room.

Thermostat dads cultivate: they bring up their children with consistency, honesty, and presence, giving real time and attention rather than gifts, and watering their own home instead of comparing it to others.

Thermostat dads elevate: they put God first and raise their children in the discipline and instruction of the Lord, treating their family as their primary ministry, and it is never too late to step into that calling.

versesMentioned.text: The tongue has the power of life and death, and those who love it will eat its fruit.
Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The old has gone, the new is here!
Start children off on the way they should go, and even when they are old they will not turn from it.
Wives, submit yourselves to your own husbands as you do to the Lord.
Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her.

Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right. "Honor your father and mother" (this is the first commandment with a promise), "that it may go well with you and that you may live long in the land." Fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, but bring them up in the discipline and instruction of the Lord.
Honor your father and your mother, so that you may live long in the land the LORD your God is giving you.

Monday.scripture: Proverbs 18:21 (NIV): "The tongue has the power of life and death, and those who love it will eat its fruit."
Monday.focus: Speaking life over your home, your work, and your future.
Monday.action: Choose one person in your home or workplace and speak one sincere, encouraging sentence to them today. Notice any negative words you say and replace them with words of life.
Monday.prayer: Lord, guard my mouth today. Help me speak life over my family, my circumstances, and my future. Change my words as you change my heart. In Jesus' name, amen.

Tuesday.scripture: Proverbs 15:1 (NIV): "A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger."
Tuesday.focus: Regulate: setting a steady, calm tone instead of reacting to the mood of the room.
Tuesday.action: Before walking into your home or workplace today, pause for one minute to pray and decide what tone you want to set. If a tense moment comes, take a slow breath and answer gently.
Tuesday.prayer: Father, make me steady and wise. Help me bring calm, truth, and grace into every room I enter instead of simply reacting. In Jesus' name, amen.

Wednesday.scripture: Ephesians 6:4 (NIV): "Fathers, do not exasperate your children; instead, bring them up in the training and instruction of the Lord."
Wednesday.focus: Cultivate: giving your presence and time, not just presents.
Wednesday.action: Set aside 20 uninterrupted minutes with a child, grandchild, or young person you influence. Put your phone away and ask them about their day.
Wednesday.prayer: Lord, show me where I have been distracted or absent. Help me give my time and attention to the people you have placed in my life. In Jesus' name, amen.

Thursday.scripture: Proverbs 22:6 (NIV): "Start children off on the way they should go, and even when they are old they will not turn from it."
Thursday.focus: Consistency and honesty in building a legacy of faith.
Thursday.action: Choose one simple, repeatable rhythm, such as a short prayer at dinner, a bedtime blessing, or reading a Bible verse together. If you are not a parent, encourage a young person in their faith. Be real about your own walk with God.
Thursday.prayer: God, help me be consistent and genuine, not just in what I say but in how I live. Let my life point others toward you. In Jesus' name, amen.

Friday.scripture: 2 Corinthians 5:17 (NIV): "Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The old has gone, the new is here!"
Friday.focus: Elevate: surrendering to God and putting him first, trusting that he makes all things new.
Friday.action: Look at your calendar and ask whether it reflects your priorities. Make one change that puts God and your family first. If there is a relationship that needs repair, take one step, such as sending a kind message or making a phone call.
Friday.prayer: Jesus, I surrender my priorities, my habits, and my past to you. Make me new and help me lead the people around me toward you. In your name, amen.

Saturday.scripture: Exodus 20:12 (NIV): "Honor your father and your mother, so that you may live long in the land the LORD your God is giving you."
Saturday.focus: Honoring others, healing family stories, and encouraging someone who needs hope.
Saturday.action: Pray for your father or a father figure, whatever your story with him has been. Then encourage one person this weekend, or invite someone to watch a message with you online or in person.
Saturday.prayer: Heavenly Father, thank you for being steady and faithful when others have not been. Heal what is broken in my family story and use me to bring hope to someone else. In Jesus' name, amen.

title: How Fathers Set the Atmosphere at Home | Change The Temperature
